items.title: Delhi protests, assaults and detentions: The 18 petitions filed before Supreme Court
items.summary: At least 15 petitions have been filed before the Supreme Court in connection with the October 10 protests and detention of those who were out on streets demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over his handling of special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the functioning of Election Commission of India (ECI). The protests called by various youth bodies and political parties in Delhi had led to large scale detentions and assault of protestors as well as journalists and lawyers on October 10 and October 11. The petitions before the Supreme Court include writ petitions, contempt proceedings, habeas corpus pleas and intervention applications challenging restrictions on public transport, alleged unlawful detentions and police action against lawyers, journalists and protesters. The petitions are listed before a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. They follow the Supreme Court's October 9 directions concerning public transport restrictions and its special sitting on October 11 , when the Court issued contempt notices and directed that peaceful public movement and the professional activities of lawyers and journalists should not be unlawfully obstructed. The Court is now examining connected proceedings concerning compliance with its earlier directions, while several other petitions seek separate relief against alleged police excesses and restrictions imposed during the protests. Some of the petitions are listed for hearing on Tuesday. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The petitions and proceedings identified so far are as follows: 1. items.title: Jammu and Kashmir High Court makes AIBE mandatory for advocates enrolled since 2009-10
items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently made it mandatory for all advocates enrolled across the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh since 2009-10 to pass the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) to be entitled to practice law. Although the Bar Council of India (BCI) had made AIBE mandatory for law graduates from 2009-10 onwards, the requirement had not been formally implemented for advocates enrolled with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The Jammu and Kashmir High Court has now directed its implementation. A notification to this effect was issued by the High Court's Registrar General MK Sharma on October 10, 2026. The notification lays down that law graduates enrolled as advocates with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, who graduated in the academic year 2009-2010 onwards, must qualify the AIBE if they have not already cleared the examination. Fresh law graduates and advocates enrolled provisionally will be granted an absolute certificate of enrolment only after passing the AIBE and producing the Certificate of Practice (COP) issued by the Bar Council of India within two years. Advocates enrolled with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh after July 1, 2010, who have already qualified the AIBE, have been directed to submit copies of their Certificates of Practice to the High Court Registry within one month. The decision follows the Full Court's October 8 decision to accept an August 19 recommendation of a Rules Committee to implement Rules 9, 10 and 11 of Chapter III, Part VI of the Bar Council of India Rules concerning the AIBE. Rule 9 of the BCI Rule stipulates that advocates must successfully pass the AIBE to be entitled to practise under Chapter IV of the Advocates Act, 1961. Rule 11 provides for the issuance of the Certificate of Practice to successful candidates. [Read Notification]

items.title: Delhi court sends CJP's Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to judicial custody for 5 days
items.summary: A Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court on Wednesday remanded Cockroach Janta Part (CJP) activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to judicial custody for 5 days. Das, Ranka along with another CJP activist Ajinkya Shinde were detained by the Delhi Police on October 13 after allegedly entering the barricaded Jantar Mantar site by climbing its gates. The CJP activists took the action a day after Jantar Mantar was de-notified as the designated protest site. While Das and Ranka were remanded to judicial custody today, Shinde was released. Notably, the CJP has been protesting alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. This is a developing story.

items.title: Homemaker’s household services cannot be ignored in accident compensation merely because she is over 70: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that while determining motor accident compensation, a homemaker’s unpaid household and caregiving services cannot be disregarded merely because she is above 70 years of age [Ganga Devi v Rajesh Kumar & Ors] . Justice Anish Dayal said that the assessment of compensation should not be founded upon stereotypes or assumptions that a person ceases to contribute merely by reason of having attained an advanced age. The Court warned against such prejudices and said that data demonstrates that women beyond the age of 70 years continue to render gratuitous services to their families, including household and caregiving services. “This Court is conscious that such contributions, particularly those rendered within the household and without monetary remuneration, are often overlooked or undervalued. However, the absence of a monetary consideration cannot operate to the advantage of the tortfeasor or diminish the compensation otherwise payable to the injured claimant,” the Bench ruled. Justice Anish Dayal Delhi High Court Data demonstrates that women beyond the age of 70 years continue to render gratuitous services to their families, including household and caregiving services. The Court made the observations while allowing an appeal filed by Ganga Devi, who was 74 when a bus accident in February 2019 crushed both her legs. She suffered 74 percent permanent disability in relation to both lower limbs. The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) awarded her ₹14.42 lakh in compensation but denied claims for loss of income and future income. The tribunal reasoned that she was an elderly woman who had never been employed and that there was insufficient evidence of her contribution to household work. However, the Court rejected this approach. It observed that such assumptions risk perpetuating age-based stereotypes, commonly described as ageism. The Court underscored that older people do not merely receive care from younger family members but also continue to provide valuable domestic assistance, including looking after grandchildren. The court noted that unpaid household work has identifiable economic value, as families would otherwise have to spend money on cooking, childcare and other domestic services. items.title: SIR: Karnataka High Court stays probe against BJP's Ravi Patil booked for attempt to delete Muslim voters
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday stayed the investigation against BJP leader Ravi Patil and two of his supporters in a case registered over the alleged attempt to delete the names of 198 Muslim voters from the electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process in Belagavi. Justice Venkatesh Naik T passed the interim order after observing that a coordinate Bench of the High Court had stayed the investigation in similar matters on October 9. Justice Venkatesh Naik T “The coordinate Bench had stayed the investigation in similar matters on 09.10.2026. The perusal of the aforesaid order and the facts and circumstances involved in the present case are similar. In view of maintaining judicial discipline, it is just and proper to stay the investigation till the next date of hearing” the Court recorded. The Court further permitted the State government to seek modification or vacation of the interim order, if necessary. Senior Advocate M Aruna Shyam During the hearing, Senior Advocate M Aruna Shyam , appearing for the petitioners, submitted that a coordinate Bench had already stayed the investigation in similar cases. On October 8, another bench of High Court had directed the police not to take any coercive steps against Ravi Patil and his two supporters. According to the FIR, the petitioners, along with around 20 to 25 other persons, allegedly conspired to target voters belonging to the Muslim community and sought the deletion of the names of 198 voters from the electoral rolls during the SIR process. The matter has been posted for further hearing on October 29.

items.title: Kerala lawyers hold symbolic impeachment of CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.summary: Lawyers from across Kerala gathered near the Kerala High Court premises on Tuesday evening to symbolically impeach Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations concerning the functioning and independence of the Election Commission of India. The assembly was organised by the Indian Association of Lawyers (IAL)with representatives from 88 court centres across the State invited to participate. The lawyers assembled in front of the Kerala High Court Advocates Association Golden Jubilee Chamber Complex at 4:30 PM holding banners and the Constitution and demanding Kumar's impeachment. They collectively recited the Preamble and passed a resolution symbolically impeaching Kumar. " The confidence of the people in the neutrality of the Election Commission, strikes at the roots of our democratic system of governance and further resolve that Sri Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioner of India, be and is hereby symbolically impeached, " the resolution stated. The lawyers also requested the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha to consider the notice of motion for Kumar's removal under Article 324 (5)read with Article 124 (4) of the Constitution and the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 so that the allegations could be examined in accordance with law in an impartial manner. This symbolic impeachment comes amid nationwide protests demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. items.title: Telangana: ECI to hold special camps on October 15, 16 to enrol missing voters
items.summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) will organise special camps on October 15 and 16 to help eligible voters missing from the draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to apply for inclusion. The initiative will also focus on first-time voters and young electors seeking registration through Form-6. The camps are part of a one-month initiative to re-include eligible voters omitted from the draft rolls. According to a memorandum issued by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Booth Level Officers (BLO) and Booth Level Agents (BLA) representing political parties will be present at the camps to assist applicants in the enrolment process. Telangana CEO Sudarshan Reddy has directed District Election Officers (DEO) and Electoral Registration Officers (ERO) to take necessary measures to aid electors. As part of the drive, BLOs have been instructed to identify individuals whose names featured in the electoral rolls before the SIR but were missing from the latest draft lists. They will conduct door-to-door visits to verify the status of such voters and help those found eligible submit Form-6 applications. Each BLO has been asked to reach at least 20–25 omitted electors every week, with the entire exercise scheduled for completion within one month. The field visits will also cover first-time voters who need assistance registering themselves. The BLOs will share the identified voters' lists, completed application forms, and field verification reports with the EROs and BLAs. Following the completion of the exercise, booth-wise lists of eligible voters missing from the draft rolls will also be provided to political party representatives to help them identify additional cases and assist eligible individuals in applying for enrolment.

items.title: ‘Peaceful protest a democratic right’: Karnataka govt to review police action on protesters
items.summary: The Karnataka government will review the police action against protesters and journalists during an anti-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) demonstration in Bengaluru on Monday, October 12. Chief Minister DK Shivakumar has sought a report on the incident and Home Minister Priyank Kharge has assured that peaceful protests would not be disrupted. Shivakumar said he had taken note of the police action against protesters and members of the media and sought a full report on the circumstances that led to it. “If there has been any unnecessary use of force or excess, accountability will follow,” he said. The Chief Minister reiterated that peaceful protest was a fundamental democratic right. “The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. We cannot demand that right for ourselves in Delhi and deny it to others in Bengaluru. Karnataka must hold itself to the democratic standards that we expect from the rest of the country. There will be no double standards,” he said in a statement on Tuesday, October 13. “Let me be clear: disagreement with the Election Commission, disagreement with my government, or disagreement with me personally does not diminish anyone’s right to peacefully express it,” Shivakumar added. The police action took place on October 12 when protesters gathered near KR Circle to march to the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of Karnataka. items.summary: Former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has approached the Bengaluru City Civil court seeking to stop 42 media organisations and digital platforms from publishing videos and related material that he says falsely connect him to a controversy involving a woman. The case came up before Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge B Pushpanjali on Monday, October 12. Siddaramaiah’s suit seeks a permanent injunction against the publication or circulation of two videos, along with clips, screenshots, transcripts and reports reproducing their allegations. He has also asked the court to direct platforms to remove the videos or block access to them. The defendants include Kannada and English newspapers, television channels, digital platforms, YouTube LLC, Google India, WhatsApp, Yahoo India and Facebook India. Siddaramaiah has described all the material telecast as false and politically motivated, arguing that its continued online circulation could cause lasting damage to his reputation.
